lead: How a beam fails depends on how much tension steel it has. With little steel the bars yield first, the beam sags and cracks widely, and people get a warning. With too much steel the concrete crushes first, suddenly. Between the two, where both happen at once, is the balanced section. IS 456 fixes that boundary as x<sub>u,max</sub> and allows only sections on the ductile side of it.
prereq: You need the force and moment equations of singly reinforced beams and the design stress-strain curves of concrete and steel.

sections.h3: Strain diagram and the three modes

blocks.text: At collapse the top fibre is at the crushing strain ε<sub>cu</sub> = 0.0035. Plane sections stay plane, so the strain in the tension steel follows from similar triangles:

blocks.where: ε<sub>s</sub> is the strain at the tension steel. A shallow neutral axis gives a large steel strain.

blocks.text: IS 456 calls the steel yielded when ε<sub>s</sub> reaches ε<sub>s,lim</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub>/E<sub>s</sub> + 0.002, with E<sub>s</sub> = 2 × 10⁵ N/mm². The extra 0.002 is where a cold-worked bar reaches 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> on its design curve. Setting ε<sub>s</sub> = ε<sub>s,lim</sub> gives the balanced depth:

items: Under-reinforced: xu < xu,max. The steel reaches εs,lim before the concrete crushes; large deflection and wide cracks give warning. Mu = 0.87 fy Ast (d − 0.42 xu).
Balanced: xu = xu,max. Steel reaches εs,lim as the concrete crushes. The moment is Mu,lim.

Over-reinforced: xu > xu,max. The concrete crushes while the steel stress is still below 0.87 fy; failure is sudden. IS 456 does not allow it in design, and in an analysis question the moment of resistance is limited to Mu,lim.

blocks.text: Some texts call these tension-controlled and compression-controlled sections; the test is still x<sub>u</sub> against x<sub>u,max</sub>, or A<sub>st</sub> against A<sub>st,lim</sub>.
At the balanced point C = T with the steel at 0.87 f<sub>y</sub>:
A<sub>st,lim</sub> = 0.36 f<sub>ck</sub> b x<sub>u,max</sub> / (0.87 f<sub>y</sub>)     p<sub>t,lim</sub> = 100 A<sub>st,lim</sub>/(b d) = 41.4 (f<sub>ck</sub>/f<sub>y</sub>)(x<sub>u,max</sub>/d)
blocks.where: A<sub>st,lim</sub> is the most tension steel a singly reinforced section may have, in mm²; p<sub>t,lim</sub> the same as a percentage of b d; 41.4 = 100 × 0.36/0.87.

blocks.text: A higher steel grade allows less steel; a stronger concrete allows more.

If 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>st</sub>/(0.36 f<sub>ck</sub> b) gives x<sub>u</sub> above x<sub>u,max</sub>, that x<sub>u</sub> is wrong: it assumed the steel was at 0.87 f<sub>y</sub>, but it has not yielded. The true x<sub>u</sub> comes from strain compatibility. Guess x<sub>u</sub>, find ε<sub>s</sub> from the strain diagram, read f<sub>s</sub> from the design curve of the bar, and compare C = 0.36 f<sub>ck</sub> b x<sub>u</sub> with T = f<sub>s</sub> A<sub>st</sub>. Raise x<sub>u</sub> if C < T, lower it if C > T, and repeat until they agree. Because f<sub>s</sub> < 0.87 f<sub>y</sub>, the true x<sub>u</sub> is smaller than the first estimate.

items: Compute x<sub>u,max</sub> and A<sub>st,lim</sub> for the grades.

If A<sub>st</sub> ≤ A<sub>st,lim</sub>, the section is under- or just balanced: x<sub>u</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>st</sub>/(0.36 f<sub>ck</sub> b) and M<sub>u</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>st</sub> (d − 0.42 x<sub>u</sub>).

If A<sub>st</sub> > A<sub>st,lim</sub>, it is over-reinforced. For a code answer, M<sub>u</sub> = M<sub>u,lim</sub>. To find the real collapse moment, solve x<sub>u</sub> by strain compatibility and take M<sub>u</sub> = 0.36 f<sub>ck</sub> b x<sub>u</sub> (d − 0.42 x<sub>u</sub>).

blocks.text: If more moment is needed, compression steel (doubly reinforced beams) raises the capacity and keeps the beam ductile. The design aids stop at pt,lim for the same reason.

examples.question: A beam 300 mm wide with an effective depth of 500 mm is made of M30 concrete and Fe500 steel. Classify the section and find its moment of resistance when (a) A<sub>st</sub> = 1500 mm² and (b) A<sub>st</sub> = 2500 mm².
steps: Steel strain ε<sub>s</sub> = 0.0035 × (500 − 201.4)/201.4 = 0.00519, above ε<sub>s,lim</sub> = 0.87 × 500/200 000 + 0.002 = 0.00418, so the steel has yielded as assumed.
(b) p<sub>t</sub> = 100 × 2500/150 000 = 1.667 % > 1.142 %: over-reinforced. The code moment of resistance is M<sub>u,lim</sub> = 300.6 kN·m.
examples.answer: (a) Under-reinforced, x<sub>u</sub> = 201.4 mm, M<sub>u</sub> = 271.1 kN·m. (b) Over-reinforced; IS 456 credits only M<sub>u,lim</sub> = 300.6 kN·m.

examples.question: For case (b) above (A<sub>st</sub> = 2500 mm²), find the true neutral axis depth and collapse moment by strain compatibility, using the IS 456 design curve for Fe500.
steps: First estimate with 0.87 f<sub>y</sub>: x<sub>u</sub> = 435 × 2500/3240 = 335.6 mm. It is above 230 mm, so the steel has not yielded and this value is not the answer.

Trial x<sub>u</sub> = 300 mm: ε<sub>s</sub> = 0.0035 × 200/300 = 0.00233, f<sub>s</sub> = 394.7 N/mm² from the curve; C = 0.36 × 30 × 300 × 300 = 972.0 kN, T = 394.7 × 2500 = 986.9 kN. C < T, so x<sub>u</sub> must grow.
Trial x<sub>u</sub> = 310 mm: ε<sub>s</sub> = 0.0035 × 190/310 = 0.00215, f<sub>s</sub> = 383.6 N/mm²; C = 1004.4 kN, T = 959.0 kN. C > T, so x<sub>u</sub> lies between 300 and 310 mm.
Converged: x<sub>u</sub> = 302.8 mm, ε<sub>s</sub> = 0.00228, f<sub>s</sub> = 392.4 N/mm²; C = T = 981.0 kN.
So 46 % more steel than A<sub>st,lim</sub> raised the collapse moment by 22 %, while the steel strain at failure fell to 0.00228, below 0.00418.
examples.answer: x<sub>u</sub> = 302.8 mm (not 335.6 mm), f<sub>s</sub> = 392.4 N/mm², true collapse moment 365.8 kN·m; the code value stays M<sub>u,lim</sub> = 300.6 kN·m because the failure is brittle.

traps: Calling a beam under-reinforced because its steel looks small. 1500 mm² is under-reinforced in the 300 × 500 M30 beam above but would be over-reinforced in a 230 × 300 M20 beam (A<sub>st,lim</sub> = 0.36 × 20 × 230 × 0.48 × 250/361.05 = 550 mm² for d = 250 mm).
Using x<sub>u,max</sub>/d = 0.48 for Fe500. The value is 0.46; with 0.48 the limiting moment of the example would be 310.4 kN·m instead of 300.6 kN·m.

Using 0.36 f<sub>ck</sub> b x<sub>u</sub> = 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> A<sub>st</sub> for an over-reinforced section. In example (b) it gives 335.6 mm against the true 302.8 mm, because the steel stress is only 392.4 N/mm², not 435 N/mm².

Taking the yield strain f<sub>y</sub>/E<sub>s</sub> as the balanced strain. IS 456 uses 0.87 f<sub>y</sub>/E<sub>s</sub> + 0.002; with f<sub>y</sub>/E<sub>s</sub> alone, x<sub>u,max</sub>/d for Fe415 would come out 0.63.
Comparing p<sub>t</sub> with a fixed value such as 1 % instead of p<sub>t,lim</sub> for the actual concrete and steel grades.

quiz.a: A section in which the tension steel reaches its limiting strain 0.87 f<sub>y</sub>/E<sub>s</sub> + 0.002 at the same moment that the concrete reaches 0.0035, so x<sub>u</sub> = x<sub>u,max</sub>.

quiz.q: Why does IS 456 not allow over-reinforced beams?
quiz.a: They fail by concrete crushing while the steel is still elastic, so there is little deflection or cracking before collapse; the extra steel buys little strength. An under-reinforced beam gives warning.

quiz.q: b = 250 mm, d = 400 mm, M25, Fe415, A<sub>st</sub> = 1100 mm². Classify the section.
quiz.a: p<sub>t</sub> = 100 × 1100/(250 × 400) = 1.10 %. p<sub>t,lim</sub> = 41.4 × (25/415) × 0.48 = 1.20 %. p<sub>t</sub> < p<sub>t,lim</sub>, so it is under-reinforced.

quiz.q: Derive x<sub>u,max</sub>/d for Fe500 from the strain diagram.
In worked example 2, the estimate with 0.87 f<sub>y</sub> gave x<sub>u</sub> = 335.6 mm. Is that estimate too deep or too shallow, and why?
quiz.a: Too deep. It puts T = 435 × 2500 = 1087.5 kN, but the steel only reaches 392.4 N/mm², so the true tension and therefore the compression block are smaller: 981.0 kN and x<sub>u</sub> = 302.8 mm.

beyond: Not for the exam. ACI 318 calls a section tension-controlled when the steel strain at failure is at least 0.005 and lowers its strength factor below that. Earthquake design looks at curvature ductility, which falls steeply as the steel approaches the balanced amount. Search for moment-curvature analysis of RC beams.

figure.caption: All three strain lines pivot on 0.0035 at the top. With 1500 mm² the neutral axis is at 201.4 mm and the steel strains past the 0.00418 limit; at 230 mm the section is balanced; with 2500 mm² the axis drops to 302.8 mm and the steel reaches only 0.00228.
